title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', the follow-up to La Longue Marche. The setting is the profinite completion of the modular group. 𝔊 denotes a profinite group of type SL(2,Z)^ or the free product Z/2 * Z/3 (i.e. PSL(2,Z)^ = 𝔖^{+∧}_{0,3}). 𝔊' is a closely related group: an extension or variant containing the twisting element τ'. ρ and σ are the standard torsion generators of order 3 and 2 (or 6 and 4 upstairs). Further notation:
- N_ρ, N_σ: normalizers of the subgroups generated by ρ and σ.
- Z_ρ, Z_σ: their centralizers.
- ε_ρ, ε_σ: signs recording whether a normalizing element sends ρ to ρ^{±1} (resp. σ to σ^{±1}), with exact sequences 1→Z→N→{±1}→1.
- B_{ρ,σ}: a group of (generalized) automorphisms.
- T_{ρ,σ}: a common quotient through which the maps δ_B, δ_ρ, δ_σ factor. It carries a multiplier character χ_T: T→Ẑ^*.
- ε_2(μ), ε_3(μ): the signs of the multiplier μ modulo 4 (or 2) and modulo 3, i.e. the parts of the cyclotomic character seen by the torsion elements.

The problem. The previous page parametrizes the solutions (α,β,μ) of the 'loop equation' lying over a given u and μ. These are the pairs that conjugate u(ρ) to a power of ρ and u(σ) to a power of σ, of the form α = u·a^{-1}·τ'^{ν_3}, β = u·b^{-1}. It finds that they form a coset under Z_ρ × Z_σ, subject to the parity constraints ε_ρ(a)=ε_3(μ) and ε_σ(b)=ε_2(μ). It then introduces the fibre product M_{ρ,σ}[0] = B ×_T N_ρ ×_T N_σ.

On this page:
- (57) The composite S_0M[0] → T → Ẑ^* is called χ, the multiplier.
- (58) There are two homomorphisms to {±1}². The first is ε_{ρ,σ} = (ε_σ, ε_ρ), the 'geometric' signs of a and b.
- (59) The second is ε_{2,3} = (ε_2∘χ, ε_3∘χ), the 'arithmetic' signs coming from the multiplier.
- (60) M^eff is defined as the coincidence subgroup (equalizer) of these two homomorphisms. Explicitly it is the set of triples (u,a,b) with δ_B(u) = δ_ρ(a) = δ_σ(b) = Δ, ε_ρ(a) = ε_3(χ(Δ)) and ε_σ(b) = ε_2(χ(Δ)).
- (61) It maps to 𝔊' × 𝔊 × Ẑ^* by (u,a,b) ↦ (u a^{-1} τ'^{ν_ρ(a)}, u b^{-1}, μ), where (−1)^{ν_ρ(a)} = ε_ρ(a). This is designed to be injective with image exactly the set SG^eff of 'effective' solutions of the loop equation.
- (62) This gives a bijection M^eff ≅ SG^eff, which transports a group structure onto the solution set: the solutions form a group, a fibre product of the automorphism group with the normalizers.
- Remark (second (62)). The same formulas define a map on all of M[0]. For a general element the resulting (α,β) still conjugate u(ρ) and u(σ) to ρ^{±1} and σ^{±1}, but the signs no longer need to match ε_2(μ), ε_3(μ).

Where this leads. The next page uses the remark to propose an overgroup of B of index 1, 2 or 4, hopefully the rational points of a group scheme over Z. It also proposes re-normalizing β by τ'^ν to remove the sign. In GT language this is the bookkeeping of the 'λ-part' (multiplier μ = cyclotomic-type character) and the 'f-part' (α, β) of the action on Π_{0,3}^∧ and on SL(2,Z)^. Here it is organized as an equalizer subgroup of a fibre product of normalizers.
errors: In (60) the explicit description has b ∈ Z_σ (centralizer). Consistency with the previous page (b ∈ N_σ with ε_σ(b)=ε_2(μ)) and with the formula itself requires b ∈ N_σ. As written, Z_σ would force ε_σ(b)=1. This is a slip.
ν_ρ(a) is said to lie in 'Z/12' while only its parity matters ((−1)^ν = ε_ρ(a)). Either a misreading of Z/2, or ν is taken mod the order of τ' with only its parity used.
Notation drifts between S_0M[0], S_0{M_{ρ,σ}} and M^eff without S_0. Equation number (62) is used twice.

The injectivity of (61) and the equality of its image with SG^eff are asserted ('on a fait ce qu'il fallait'), not proved on this page. Recovering u from (α,β,μ) depends on how B sits inside the ambient group.

ideas.what: Parametrizing solutions of the loop equation (images of the order-2 and order-3 generators under an automorphism of the profinite modular group) by a fibre product of the automorphism group with the normalizers N_ρ, N_σ over a common quotient T
ideas.modern_name: Torsor/group structure on solutions of the GT-type relations (Grothendieck–Teichmüller group as automorphisms of SL(2,Z)^ / Π_{0,3}^ preserving the conjugacy classes of torsion)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for GT; Ihara; Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura (actions on the profinite modular group)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche discuss Gal(Q̄/Q) acting on fundamental groups of moduli and the 'équation des lacets' only programmatically; this detailed fibre-product construction is unpublished as far as I know

ideas.what: Equalizer ('sous-groupe des coïncidences') of the geometric signs (ε_ρ, ε_σ) and the arithmetic signs (ε_2∘χ, ε_3∘χ) of the multiplier, defining the 'effective' subgroup
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the cyclotomic character mod 3 and mod 4 with the conjugation action on elliptic elements of SL(2,Z)^
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in the GT / Galois action on PSL(2,Z)^ literature (action on order-2 and order-3 elements via λ)

ideas.what: Observation that dropping the sign constraint yields a larger group containing B with index 1, 2 or 4, possibly the rational points of a group scheme over Z (developed on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Enlarging GT-type groups by sign/orientation twists; arithmetic (scheme-theoretic) models of such groups

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a group structure on the set of effective solutions of the loop equation through a fibre product of normalizers. He then signals (remark, continued on the next page) a larger group of index ≤4 that he hopes is the rational points of a group scheme over Z. That scheme-theoretic thread is not carried out here.
missed.quote: Remarques En fait (61) les formules par ... une application M_{ρ,σ}[0] → 𝔊'×𝔊×Ẑ^*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor variant of the known structure of GT acting on the profinite modular group. A group-scheme-over-Z model of a GT-type group is not standard, but here it is only a hope, not a construction.

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful bookkeeping in Grothendieck's independent pre-Drinfeld-style analysis of the 'équation des lacets': signs, normalizers, and a fibre-product group identified with the solution set. It is historically interesting as part of the unpublished GT-anticipating material, but the content on this page is technical and its structure is essentially recoverable from the later GT literature.
transcription_corrections: In (60), 'b ∈ Z_σ' matches the manuscript but is a mathematical slip for N_σ.
'ν_ρ(a) ∈ Z/12' is likely 'Z/2' (only the parity is used).
The next page's number reads '575' in the transcription; it should be 545 in sequence.
In (58) the subscript in ε_{ρ,σ} = (ε_σ, ε_ρ) is overwritten in the manuscript; the ordering matching (ε_2, ε_3) in (59) is plausible.
Before (61), 'On a une application naturelle' is correct. The NB about ν_ρ is written in the left margin, with '(−1)^{ν_ρ(a)} = ε_ρ(a)'.
